pdp.title: Thyreogen | Thyroid Peptide Bioregulator
overview: Thyreogen® is a natural peptide complex (A-2) derived from thyroid gland tissue, part of the Khavinson Cytomax® line of organ-specific peptide bioregulators.

It is believed to support normal thyroid function and the body's metabolic balance. Thyreogen is taken orally as capsules and is often considered by adults who want to support their endocrine system as they age.
pdp.why: The thyroid is a butterfly-shaped gland at the front of the neck. Its hormones set the pace of metabolism: how quickly the body uses energy, keeps warm and supports heart rate, mood and weight. Small changes in thyroid activity can be felt throughout the body.
interest: Thyroid tissue peptides and thyroid cell activity in laboratory models
Metabolic regulation by the endocrine system
How hormone-producing tissue changes with age
pdp.interestNote: These are areas of biological investigation, not guarantees of clinical benefit.
differences: Bonothyrk is the parathyroid complex (A-21); the parathyroid glands sit next to the thyroid but regulate calcium rather than metabolism.
Glandokort (adrenal, A-17) targets another endocrine gland.
Thyreogen does not contain thyroid hormone and is not a substitute for thyroid medication.
Cytomax® products are natural peptide complexes extracted from the corresponding organ tissue of young animals.

pdp.researchBackground: Thyreogen belongs to a family of short peptide bioregulators developed by researchers associated with Prof. Vladimir Khavinson at the St. Petersburg Institute of Bioregulation and Gerontology. Researchers have investigated how short peptides from specific tissues may interact with the cells of that tissue and influence gene activity, mostly in cell and animal studies. Much of this work has been published in Russian-language literature, and we are not aware of published controlled human trials of Thyreogen itself, so the research is best read as background rather than proof of effect.
